title: Input: Improve multiplayer support by implementing `PlayerID`

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Partially supersedes #102412.
Implements some parts of https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10070.

## Goal

The main goal is to easily distinguish input events for different players through code, instead of relying on input map assignments (where you’d normally create a separate action for each player mapped to a different device).
This also allows you to share devices (like a keyboard) between multiple players with just a bit of code tweaking.
Compatibility is preserved by using defult arguments.

## How to use it

```gdscript
# Player 1.
if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept", false, PLAYER_ID_P1): # Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept", false) is equivalent.
    print("P1 ui_accept just pressed")

# Player 2.
if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept", false, PLAYER_ID_P2):
    print("P2 ui_accept just pressed")

# Assign device 0 to player 2.
Input.set_joy_player_id(0, PLAYER_ID_P2)
```

## Content

This PR is based on @coffeebeats proposal [Improve local multiplayer support by tracking InputEvents and UI focus per player](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10070).
The author stated in the discussion:

> I think there are two sub-problems here: (1) segmenting input by player via a "player layer" and (2) allowing the engine to track UI focus for each player individually.

Only point 1 will be addressed in this PR (while point 2 will be eventually discussed and implemented in a future PR):
1. Introducing a new `player` layer between the device and game logic;

The max amount of players allowed is 8.

## Changes

* `PlayerID` is a new enum class that is used to assign and check inputs to different players;
* Methods like `Input::is_action_pressed` now have new `PlayerID` optional parameter to check which player emitted the input;
* `InputMap` action events binded to joypad devices are now set to `ALL_DEVICES` by default. This is because now the common practice to filter players is to use `PlayerID`. The possibility of choosing from `InputMap` the device id for the event is preserved to allow custom behaviours, but it is not intended as the common use case;
* Keyboard, mouse, and touch inputs can be assigned to players other than `P1` through `keyboard_player_id_override`, `mouse_player_id_override`, `touch_player_id_override`;
* When a new device is connected, a `PlayerID` is assigned to it in a cumulative way (device 0 -> P1, device 1 -> P2);
